text: You're customizing the Incident list view for the Service Desk team. Four things before the morning shift: add a Caller column, filter to active incidents assigned to Service Desk, group the result by priority, and confirm what related lists a team member would actually see on one of those incidents.

Step one. Right-click a column header, choose List Layout, move Caller from the available side into the shown-columns list, and position it right after Short description. Save. The list now shows Caller in that position for everyone using this view. No incident record changed — only the layout of this view did.

Step two. Open the condition builder. Set Active is true, add a second row, Assignment group is Service Desk, and confirm the toggle between them is AND, not OR. Run. The breadcrumb trail now reads Active is true AND Assignment group is Service Desk. Underneath, that's the same thing as the encoded query from Lesson 21 — you just built it visually.

Step three. Right-click the Priority column header and choose Group By. The filtered list reorganizes into clusters — Priority 1 first, then Priority 2, and so on. The Step 2 filter is still fully in effect; grouping only changes how those same records are presented, so a lead can spot any Priority 1 incidents immediately.

Step four. Opening one incident and scrolling down shows Affected CIs, Related Problems, and Approvals. An incident with no linked Problem record simply shows an empty Related Problems list, not a missing one — the related list is still configured; its query just returned zero rows for this incident.

Layout, a two-condition AND filter, grouping without touching records, and related-list literacy — that combination is exactly what a Service Desk admin runs through every morning. Next up: Chapter 6 begins, starting with an overview of Import Sets.
